idiom_name: class with constructor-injected read-only collaborators; object declaration or top-level functions when there is nothing to inject
implementation_notes: Kotlin expresses the service as a class whose collaborators are private val constructor properties, which is the whole classic structure - no framework construct is needed and there is no boilerplate around it. When there is nothing to inject, an object declaration or top-level functions in a services file remove the ceremony, and a single-operation service can be a fun interface implemented by a lambda, which also makes test doubles trivial. Spring's @Component works exactly as in Java when container-managed transactions or security are required, but the domain class itself stays a plain class with no framework annotations.
pitfalls: val prevents reassignment but not mutation: a MutableMap cache held as a property is still shared state across the container's singleton scope.
Capturing a CoroutineScope or a dispatcher in a service is hidden state and a leak; let callers own structured concurrency and keep the operation a suspend function.
An object declaration is initialised once per class loader and shared by every thread, so any var inside it is global mutable state.
